why: The ratchet for tools/harness/backendDiff.js. Per configuration, how many of the 128 signature values differ beyond the noise floor between WebGL2 and WebGPU rendering the SAME scene. 0 means the two backends are pixel-identical for that configuration. A number may only go DOWN: this file records how far apart they are today, and refuses to let them drift further, without ever claiming the current difference is correct. Lower an entry in the commit that earns it; raising one needs a reason written next to it. Motion-dependent configurations are excluded — they are phase-dependent and no seed fixes that. RAISED 2026-08-27, one reason: WebGPU had no usable mip chain on any cube it rendered itself. `generateMipmaps` submitted a private encoder while the passes that drew level 0 were still unsubmitted in the frame encoder, so every level above the first was built from a level nothing had written. Both cubes were affected — the probe capture and the sky atmosphere bake. The probe inspector preview measured mean luminance 0.0 against WebGL2 s 110.6, and `prefilter.wgsl`, which samples the source cube at a roughness-derived mip, returned black for every roughness above 0. The chain is real now and agrees with WebGL2 to 0.2 in mean luminance, differing in ~7% of pixels concentrated at cube-face borders. These entries record THAT residual. They went up because a term that was missing came back, not because the backends drifted: a zero here previously meant both backends agreed on nothing, which is exactly the false green the paragraph above warns about. LOWERED 2026-08-28, deferred.every, nine entries — several now BELOW where they sat before silhouette clipping existed (ssao/chromatic/noShadows back to 0). The 2026-08-27 raise was for a hard `discard` threshold on the output of a ray march, which is the most divergence-amplifying construct in this pipeline. Clipped materials are now depth-bounded (parallaxBoundedDepth / POM_CLIP_REACH), so the lateral travel — and with it the band of fragments sitting near the threshold where a sub-ULP difference flips the discard — is capped. The ratchet is supposed to fall when a change earns it, and this one did; these are recorded values, not estimates. RAISED 2026-08-28, deferred.every, one reason: the `every` scene GAINED CONTENT. It now carries a displaced subdivided cube and a displaced sphere (24 -> 150 and 625 -> 2401 vertices), added so that vertex displacement is not shipped ungated — a bake nothing exercises is a bake nothing tests. Roughly 24k extra triangles, and on WebGPU they are displaced by a COMPUTE DISPATCH while WebGL2 runs the JS executor, so these entries record two things at once and it is worth saying which is which. It was measured rather than assumed, by forcing the CPU executor on both backends (`?cpudisplace=1`, see DisplacementBaker): with both on JS the same configurations differ in 3/128, 4/128 and 1/128 cells; with the dispatch they differ in 6, 6 and 5. So the compute path adds differing CELLS, not larger errors — the worst per-cell delta is 8/255 in BOTH configurations, which is the noise this scene already has between backends, not an executor disagreement. Had the dispatch silently done nothing, WebGPU would have drawn flat cubes against displaced ones and the deltas would have been an order of magnitude larger, not the same number. LOWERED 2026-08-28 (later the same day), deferred.every, THIRTEEN entries — every one of them, and eight straight back to 0. This reverses the raise logged immediately above: the displaced cube and sphere that paid for it have been DELETED. Vertex displacement is now terrain-only — an ordinary mesh cannot displace, because its vertices are what `Model.serialize()` writes and there is no primitive descriptor in the persistence path to rebuild them from, so a bake would be saved over the authored asset. Terrain rebuilds its vertices from a height field it owns and never serializes them, so it can. With the two meshes gone the compute executor they exercised is gone with them (`displaceCompute.wgsl`, and the `?cpudisplace=1` A/B flag the note above refers to), and the scene is back to one executor on both backends. What replaced them is a displaced TERRAIN layer in the same scene, which bakes in JS on both backends and therefore adds no cross-backend divergence of its own. These are recorded values, not estimates. RAISED 2026-08-28 (third entry that day), deferred.every, ONE entry — debugSSAO, 0 -> 1, worst per-cell delta 8/255. Terrain relief is now geometry only, and its depth is finally in the right unit (tiled uv converted by `size / tiling` rather than treated as raw metres), so the scene's terrain carries roughly 3x the relief it did — and SSAO reads derivatives, so it is the one configuration sensitive enough to notice. It was MEASURED rather than assumed: forcing both backends onto the CPU executor gives 0/128 differing at worst delta 4, i.e. the recorded 0 still holds; with the compute dispatch it is 1/128 at worst 8. So this single cell is a CPU-vs-compute residual, not the deeper relief. Its cause is known and bounded: the compute path samples the PACKED layer texture's GPU mips while the CPU path samples a mip pyramid it builds from the RAW height map, and `TexturePacker` sizes a pack as the max of its sources — so the two read the same field through slightly different filtering. One cell at the noise magnitude this scene already carries. Binding the raw height texture to the dispatch would close it; not done, and recorded here so the next person knows the residual has a name. ADJUSTED 2026-08-28 (fourth entry that day), deferred.every, two entries and they moved in opposite directions. Terrain relief is now CENTRED on its height map's mean rather than added on top of the sculpted surface — parallax could only carve INTO a surface, so replacing it with pure addition had been lifting every painted region by one mean amplitude and reading as inverted relief. LOWERED debugSSAO 1 -> 0: centring roughly halves the peak displacement in this scene (max delta 0.129 -> 0.041 m), and the CPU-vs-compute residual recorded there last time is now below the noise floor. RAISED base 1 -> 2, worst per-cell delta 8/255, and it was MEASURED before being written down: forcing both backends onto the CPU executor leaves it at 2/128 as well, so this one is NOT an executor disagreement — it is the centred relief itself, which is a deliberate change to what the scene looks like. The same run confirms the attribution in the other direction: debugSSAO drops to 0/128 only when the dispatch is disabled, which is what identifies it as the executor residual. RAISED 2026-08-28 (fifth entry that day), twelve entries across deferred.base, deferred.every and forward.every, EVERY ONE of them +1 to +3 differing CELLS at a worst per-cell delta of 8/255, which is the noise this scene already carries between backends. Lights went photometric: one radiance colour times an intensity in lux or lumens, and a windowed inverse-square falloff, replacing `diffuse` and `1 / (c + l*d + q*d^2)`. What widened is the DYNAMIC RANGE of the intermediate, not the math. Legacy content asserts a lamp is as bright at 1 m as the sun, so the mesh scene's migrated lamp carries ~4.2 Mlm, which reaches the shader as a candela around 4 and is then multiplied by an attenuation around 1e-2 — where the old form multiplied an O(1) colour by an O(1e-2) attenuation. A product spanning more decades is associated differently by the two compilers, and a quantised cell mean sitting on a boundary flips. The attribution is in which profiles moved: forward.base and forward.full are ALL PASS and both are lit, so the BRDF and the falloff agree between backends; what moves is deferred, and within it the configurations that resample or composite (halfScale, grid, godRays, combined). A prediction worth checking when the harness pages are rewritten in native units — planned as its own commit, deliberately not this one, so that the migration path is what these numbers measure: these entries should fall back, because a 1500 lm lamp does not span the same decades. If they do not, the explanation above is wrong and this needs a real investigation. RAISED 2026-08-28 (sixth entry that day), sixteen entries across deferred.every, forward.every and deferred.every2d, every one of them +1 to +3 differing CELLS at a worst per-cell delta of 8/255 (the exception, deferred.every noShadows at 12, is 4 cells). The specular BRDF became energy-conserving: height-correlated Smith VISIBILITY replacing the separable geometry term and its `+ 0.001` denominator epsilon, Burley diffuse replacing Lambert, the `(1 - F)` factor dropped from the diffuse lobe, and Kulla-Conty multi-scatter compensation added to both direct light and IBL. THE CAUSE WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, because the obvious suspect was wrong. `exp2` is the one new intrinsic this change puts on the lighting path (inside Karis EnvBRDFApprox), it had never round- tripped through the generated GLSL chunk before, and the plan predicted the divergence would be there. It is not: neutering `energyCompensation` to return 1 and rebuilding leaves the rise in place and makes several entries WORSE (deferred.every skyFog 1 -> 4 with compensation off versus 1 -> 4 with it on; godRays 3 -> 5 with it off, and it does not appear at all with it on). So the churn is the visibility and diffuse terms, which are arithmetic the two compilers are free to associate differently, not a new builtin behaving differently. The attribution is in which profiles did NOT move: forward.base, forward.full and forward.every2d are ALL PASS, and all three are lit. The BRDF itself therefore agrees between backends; what moved is the heaviest scenes, where a longer expression tree (two sqrts and a divide per light where there used to be a multiply) puts more cells within one quantisation step of a bucket boundary. Same phenomenon as the phase-1 raise logged above, same magnitude, different arithmetic. These are recorded values, not estimates. RAISED 2026-08-28 (seventh entry that day), three entries, +1 to +2 differing CELLS at a worst per-cell delta of 8/255. Lights gained physical SIZE: Karis representative-point sphere lights for point and spot, the reflection ray clamped into the sun's cone for the directional, and the `(alpha/alphaPrime)^2` energy correction on both. The new arithmetic is a `normalize` of a vector that shrinks to zero as the reflection ray passes through the source centre, which is the one genuinely new numerical hazard on this path and the first suspect for any divergence here. Two things are worth recording alongside the numbers, because they are unusual. First, the raise is smaller than the change: at the SHIPPED default sizes (a 5 cm bulb, the real sun) this phase is invisible to an 8x8 quantised signature — measured, not assumed. Toggling a 5 cm `sourceRadius` between 0.05 and 0 moves ZERO of the 128 values even against a mirror-finish sphere; 0.5 m moves zero; a full 1 m bulb moves two. Second, and consequently, the mesh page now authors a 0.5 m bulb and a sun twenty times life size. Those exist for COVERAGE, not for a gate: they make the code execute on a real driver every run, which is what catches a NaN or a shader that stops compiling, but they do not pin its numerics. A future regression in the representative-point math would not be caught by any gate in this repo. That is stated plainly here rather than left to be discovered. LOWERED 2026-08-28 (eighth entry that day), twenty-one entries across deferred.every and forward.every — nine and twelve, several of them straight back to 0. Terrain gained AMBIENT OCCLUSION: it hardcoded ao = 1, so it took full ambient everywhere while a mesh beside it got cavity darkening, and the every scene now paints a 0 -> 1 occlusion ramp on its base terrain layer. The reason this LOWERS the ratchet rather than raising it is worth stating, because the intuition points the other way. Nothing about the arithmetic changed — the occlusion is one multiply against a term both backends already computed identically. What changed is the terrain ambient MAGNITUDE: multiplying it by a mean of roughly 0.5 halves the size of the disagreement the two backends already had there, and a residual that used to sit one quantisation step above the noise floor now sits below it. So these entries are not evidence that the backends agree better; they are evidence that the terrain is darker. If a later change removes the occlusion map from the fixture, expect them to climb straight back and do not read that as a regression. The forward profile fell furthest (35 -> 29 on seven configurations) for the same reason and more of it: forward multiplies ambient by occlusion directly in terrainForward.wgsl, with no G-buffer round trip in between. These are recorded values, not estimates. ADJUSTED 2026-08-28, deferred.every, four entries — base 5->4 and halfScale 3->2 DOWN, debugScene 2->3 and debugSSAO 0->1 UP. All four are the same cause and NONE of them is an executor disagreement, which was measured rather than assumed: forcing both backends onto the CPU executor gives byte-identical counts (base 4, debugScene 3, halfScale 2, debugSSAO 1, worst delta 8 throughout). Identical either way means the JS bake and the compute dispatch now agree exactly — which is the point, because they previously did NOT: the CPU read height-map rows top-down out of `getImageData` while every image upload is flipped (`UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL, !this._flipY`), so the two bakes disagreed on which row `v = 0` is. `heightField` now draws the image upside down, so the relief is no longer mirrored against the albedo it belongs to. The cell counts moved because the terrain genuinely looks different — flipped relief, depth in world metres instead of tiled uv, and one baked density of 4 for the whole terrain instead of a per-chunk density that varied with distance. That last one is also why displacement stopped costing anything when the camera moves. LOWERED 2026-08-28 (ninth entry that day), thirteen entries across forward.every and deferred.every2d. Geometric specular antialiasing: the sub-pixel variance of the shading normal is folded into the NDF width, so roughness is WIDENED wherever the normal turns fast in screen space. It falls for the same reason terrain occlusion made it fall — the change removes high-frequency specular, and high-frequency specular is what the two compilers disagree about. Both sets were measured TWICE, identically, before being written down: these are not the plus-or-minus-one boundary flicker that deferred.base halfScale/grid show (they reported IMPROVED 1 -> 0 in the same sweep and were deliberately NOT lowered, because they wobble). every2d is in the list because it is built on top of the base scene, so it carries the PBR cube, sphere and floor behind its orthographic tile camera; the sphere at 0.25 roughness is smooth enough to filter. If a later change turns specularAaEnabled off by default, expect all thirteen to climb back, and do not read that as a regression. ADJUSTED 2026-08-28 (tenth entry that day), deferred.every, three entries: debugAO 0 -> 4 (worst per-cell delta 12/255) and combined 0 -> 1 (worst 8) UP, debugSSAO 1 -> 0 DOWN. Terrain relief is no longer geometry-only. The half of a height map too fine for the vertex grid is handed back to the parallax march as a RESIDUAL instead of being discarded, which at the editor defaults is nearly all of it: 200 m at resolution 129, density 4 and tiling 20 cuts at mip 5.32, so the geometry received a 26x26 reduction of a 1024 map and everything above that reached nothing. The two entries that rose are NOT the same kind of movement, and the difference was measured rather than assumed, by forcing both backends onto the CPU executor. `combined` sits at 1/128 at worst 8 EITHER WAY, so it is not an executor disagreement — it is the marched residual itself, which is a deliberate change to what this scene looks like. `debugAO` returns to 0/128 with the dispatch disabled, so it IS the CPU-vs-compute residual, and what changed is not that residual but its VISIBILITY. Its cause is already named further up this log: the compute bake samples the PACKED layer texture's GPU mips while the JS bake builds a pyramid from the RAW height map, and `TexturePacker` sizes a pack as the max of its sources. The march amplifies it, because a slightly different baked surface gives a slightly different view vector, which moves where the ray lands — and AO is now read at the marched uv rather than the geometric one. Binding the raw height texture to the dispatch would still close it; still not done, and the reason it is worth doing has just gone up. debugSSAO fell in all three runs of this sweep, including both halves of the A/B, so it is recorded rather than left wobbling. One thing this sweep did NOT move, which is worth saying because it was the largest fix of the round: `buildLodIndices` no longer multiplies its step by the density (at density 4 the default step of 2 became a vertex step of 8, coarser than the height grid itself, so every chunk past 120 m decimated away the entire sub-grid band). The `every` terrain is a single chunk drawn at LOD 0, so no configuration here exercises it. These are recorded values, not estimates. ADJUSTED 2026-08-28 (eleventh entry that day), deferred.every, four entries and THREE OF THEM FELL: debugAO 4 -> 0, combined 1 -> 0, skyFog 2 -> 1, and base 4 -> 5. The GPU bake is DELETED. Terrain layer displacement ran in JS on WebGL2 and as a compute dispatch on WebGPU, and that asymmetry was the single largest source of divergence this file has ever recorded — it just could not be seen, because the fixture's height map was a 32x32 LINEAR RAMP and any two filters agree on a ramp. Giving the fixture a real 256-texel noise map (needed for a separate reason: the parallax march was inert against a ramp, since `residualHeight`'s two taps landed on the same mip) took fifteen configurations out at once, debugAO to 24/128 differing cells at a WORST DELTA OF 100/255. Forcing both backends onto the JS bake took that same entry to 0/128 and cleared fourteen of the fifteen, which is what identified the cause rather than the symptom: the two bakes ran the same ALGORITHM over DIFFERENT DATA. `tests/terrainDisplaceParity.test.ts` compared JS against a transcription of the WGSL and passed throughout, because it fed both sides the same field — precisely what they never shared in practice. The dispatch sampled the PACKED layer texture's GPU-generated mips; the JS bake builds its own pyramid from the RAW height map, and `TexturePacker` sizes a pack as the max of its sources. What made deleting it affordable rather than a regression is that the bake no longer runs on the camera path at all: relief is baked once at chunk build and again only on a sculpt, a paint stroke or a layer change, so the dispatch was optimising something that happens a handful of times in a session. Gone with it: terrainDisplaceCompute.wgsl, the hand-packed 240-byte uniform block, five texture bindings, `_displaceOnGpu` / `recordDisplaceDispatch` / `needsDisplaceDispatch` / `displaceKey` / `_heightsBuffer`, the renderer's `frame.terrainDisplace` stage, this driver's which-executor-ran gate, and the parity test whose whole subject was the deleted WGSL. The one entry that ROSE is base 4 -> 5 at a worst delta of 8/255, the noise band this scene already carries: the `every` terrain now draws a marched residual it did not draw before, which is new visible content and a deliberate change. All four were measured TWICE, identically, before being written down. If a GPU bake is ever wanted back, the fix it needs is known: upload the CPU's own pyramid as a storage buffer and index it exactly as `sampleHeightLod` does, so both sides read the same bytes. Sampling the packed texture is what cannot be made to agree. ADJUSTED 2026-08-28 (twelfth entry that day), forward.every, twelve entries: EIGHT up by one or two (base, ssao, grid, skyFog, chromatic, combined +1; noShadows, debugScene +2; from a band of 23-36 differing cells) and FOUR down (halfScale 31 -> 30, debugCascades 38 -> 37, godRays 28 -> 27, bloom 25 -> 24) — +10 and -4, a net of +6 on a profile that was already at 362. Same cause as the eleventh entry, seen through the pipeline that is most sensitive to it. This scene's terrain now carries a REAL height map — 256 texels of three-octave noise, where the fixture had been a 32x32 linear ramp — and draws a marched residual over it, which is new visible content rather than new arithmetic. forward moves more than deferred here for the reason already recorded in the eighth entry above: `terrainForward.wgsl` multiplies ambient by occlusion directly, with no G-buffer round trip in between, so a change to what the terrain looks like reaches the composite more directly. The numbers are also large to begin with in this profile — 23 to 31 of 128 at worst deltas of 36 to 60 — so a plus-one is churn within a band that was already wide, not a new class of disagreement. Measured TWICE, identically, before being written down: the same eight configurations failed and the same three improved in both runs. Worth stating for whoever looks next: forward.every totals roughly 362 across 25 configurations and has for some time. It is the one profile in this file that deserves a real investigation on its own terms, and nothing in this round's work created it. RAISED 2026-08-29, and it is two separate causes recorded together because they arrived in one change. FIRST, BLOOM STARTED WORKING: deferred.base, forward.base, deferred.full, deferred.every and forward.every all move from 0 to between 18 and 50 differing cells, plus debugBloom on the two forward profiles. A recorded 0 there did NOT mean the backends agreed - it meant the bright pass was reading an unwritten mip level of the compose buffer and emitting nothing, so the two backends agreed on nothing, which is exactly the false green this file warns about at the top. `_compose_FBOs` was the one render target in the renderer created without `mipMap: false`, so `Texture` defaulted it to true and gave it `linear-mipmap-linear` over a chain nothing generates; present samples it 1:1 at LOD 0 and looked perfect, while the bright pass halves the resolution and its implicit LOD landed on level 1. With that fixed, bloom is a six-level float mip pyramid with a tent filter on every level, which is a long expression tree the two compilers are free to associate differently. SECOND, AUTO-EXPOSURE, a new configuration rather than a raise, and its numbers are large: 78 to 118 differing cells across the profiles. The cause is structural rather than a defect, and worth stating so nobody spends a day on it. Auto-exposure is a CLOSED LOOP over the whole frame: it meters the scene to a single average, and that one number multiplies every pixel. So the two to five cells the backends already disagree about in an ordinary frame become a small difference in the metered average, and the metered average then shifts the ENTIRE image - one local disagreement amplified into a global one. It is NOT quantisation: the metering readback was widened from 8 to 16 bits (two channels of the 1x1 target rather than one) specifically to test that hypothesis, and the number did not move at all, 108/128 before and after. It is deterministic, measured identically on three consecutive runs. Any future change that reduces the underlying per-pixel divergence should pull all of these down together. RAISED 2026-08-29 (second entry that day), ONE entry: forward.base autoExposure, 108 to 110 differing cells at a worst delta of 60, measured identically twice. The metering changed from a flat average log-luminance over the frame to a 10/90 percentile mean, matching Unreal's AutoExposureLow/HighPercent defaults, so the two backends now settle on very slightly different exposures than before - and because exposure multiplies every pixel, two more cells cross the floor. Same amplification the original entry describes; nothing new is wrong. Worth recording alongside it: the percentile change is honest but NOT a measured win on this fixture. Against a flat average it moves the exposure by 0.04 stops when a blown emissive object enters the frame (0.21 versus 0.25) and by 0.03 when a large dark object does (1.19 versus 1.16). The dark case dominates and SHOULD - the floor covers far more than a tenth of the frame, so no percentile cut can reject it, and a genuinely dark scene ought to open up. The rejection earns its place on a small blown highlight, which this scene does not have. It costs nothing measurable: the tap count doubled to 512 in a single fragment and the frame time is unchanged at 13.35 ms.
